title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 6)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »).

sentences.en: In September, it's back to school.

sentences.fr: Les [en]f[an]ts achètent des cahiers et des crayons.
sentences.en: The children buy notebooks and pencils.

sentences.fr: Elle est très g[en]tille et elle parle l[en]tem[en]t.
sentences.en: She's very kind and she speaks slowly.

sentences.fr: Mon ami Laur[en]t est d[an]s ma classe : je suis cont[en]t !
sentences.en: My friend Laurent is in my class: I'm happy!
